title: Block 1 Revision Sheet
source: ICT Grade 3 (Nile International) revision sheet with model answers

scenes.t: When we comment on a friend's work, we use Two Stars and a Wish.
Star one: I liked your clear explanation. Star two: Your pictures were helpful.
A wish: maybe you could add more information about staying safe online.

items.q: What is an online discussion?
o: Sharing ideas and information on the internet

items.q: Which of these is a benefit of online discussions?
What does Netiquette mean?
Which information should you NOT share publicly?
What is an avatar?
o: A digital representation of a person
A file attached to a post

items.q: What is your digital footprint?
o: Information and activities you leave behind online

items.q: Which button would you use to enter an account you already have?
What should you do when you finish using a shared computer?
o: Give your password to a friend

items.q: What is a thread?
o: A specific conversation within a forum

items.q: What does embed mean?
Which of these is an example of cyberbullying?
o: Sending repeated threatening or mean messages

items.q: A picture or digital representation of you online is called an ___.
Your name, bio and picture can be part of your ___.
An online board where people discuss different subjects is a ___.
A file added to a post is called an ___.
To answer someone's comment, you can ___.
You can ___ a post if you want to change something.
The information you leave behind when using the internet is your ___.

activities.title: Match It: Block 1
activities.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.
pairs: A file added to a post
Insert media directly into a post

activities.title: True or False: Block 1
activities.prompt: Catch each sentence and send it to True or False!
items: You should respect other people's opinions online.
It is safe to share your password with your online friends.
An avatar must always be a real photograph of your face.
You should think before responding to an online message.
Using ALL CAPITAL LETTERS can look like shouting.
You should ask permission before posting a friend's photo.
You should leave your account open on a public computer.
Everything you post online can contribute to your digital footprint.
